name: Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznan
summary: Poznan university founded in 1919 with 21 faculties; nine English-taught bachelor's, from Chemistry to Liberal Arts, one at its Słubice campus.

handoff.label: AMU bachelor's degrees taught in English

ib.text: IB grades convert to Matura percentages (7 = 100%, 6 = 90%, 5 = 75%; HL counts as extended level). IB holders skip the foreigners' entrance exam, and the Diploma proves English.

programmes.name: Chemistry
programmes.about: General chemistry in English: analytical, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry, chemical technology and instrumental and spectral analysis, with much of the work done in the lab.
programmes.overview: The degree has a general academic profile and builds a broad grounding in analytical, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry, with further study of chemical technology, instrumental analysis, spectral methods and crystallochemistry. Specialisation is in general chemistry rather than a narrow branch. Graduates find work in the chemical industry, in chemical and analytical laboratories, in quality control, in research centres, in product development and in companies supplying equipment and reagents.

needs.note: Best one scores up to 60 of 100 pts; Chemistry weighs most, HL counts double SL
Up to 20 of 100 pts; HL counts double SL

programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on IB grades as Matura %: native language 20, English 20, best science 60 of 100. 25 places in the 2026 first round. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: European Legal Studies
programmes.about: How European integration shapes law, the economy and daily life: human rights, EU trade and consumer law, data protection and intellectual property, with focus tracks in law, business and society in year three.
programmes.overview: Compulsory courses include introduction to international law, philosophy of law, the European Convention on Human Rights, international protection of human rights, freedom of speech and its limits, free movement and migration policy in the EU, EU trade and consumer law, intellectual property, judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters, private international law and data protection. In the third year you choose a focus track on issues in law, business and society, and electives range from EU criminal law and food law to sectoral energy and telecommunications law and European identity. Graduates apply European law knowledge in public bodies, economic institutions and private business, including in their home countries.

needs.note: Best one scores up to 40 of 100 pts; HL counts double SL
A modern foreign language scores up to 30 of 100 pts

programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on IB grades as Matura %: native language 30, foreign language 30, history or maths 40 of 100; B2 English. 60 places in 2026. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Central European and Balkan Studies
programmes.about: Literature, languages and cultures of Central Europe and the Balkans, taught through Polish studies, Slavic studies and classical philology, with practical communication for cultural tourism and business.
programmes.overview: The programme rests on three modules: Polish language education, Slavistics and classical philology, topped up with skills in intercultural communication for tourism and business. It is aimed at people who want to work with the cultures and languages of Central Europe and the Balkans. Graduates can work in European cultural institutions such as museums, community centres, publishers and theatres, in radio, television and online media, in marketing and advertising, and in tourism, airlines and hotels.
programmes.ib: Places go by an English interview testing B2 level (pass mark 11 of 20), not by IB grades.
programmes.selectionNote: A competency interview in English decides entry; at least 11 of 20 points. 30 places in the 2026 first round. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: English Linguistics: Theories, Interfaces, Technologies
programmes.about: Theoretical and experimental linguistics (phonology, syntax, psycholinguistics, sociolinguistics) combined with language technology: text processing, language databases and speech analysis, plus academic English and internships.
programmes.overview: Study is organised in four areas: theoretical linguistics (phonology, syntax, psycholinguistics, sociolinguistics, language acquisition, cognitive linguistics), interdisciplinary linguistics with research methods, experimental work and field studies, language technology such as text processing, building language databases and speech analysis, and academic English covering pronunciation, discourse, grammar and public speaking. Training includes placements in companies. Graduates go into firms working with language data and language technologies, editorial and media work, PR, advertising, translation, education, market and opinion research, and journalism.

needs.note: Scores 70 of 100 pts; only an HL grade counts
Best one (or your native language) scores 30 of 100 pts; only HL counts

programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on IB HL grades as Matura %: English 70, plus native language or a science or maths 30 of 100. 30 places in the 2026 first round. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: International Relations
programmes.about: War, peace, conflict and cooperation between states: international law, economics, diplomacy, negotiation and foreign policy, with specialties in Geopolitics and Strategic Studies or Global Economy and International Business.
programmes.overview: Alongside comparative politics, the programme looks at intercultural communication, political campaigns, media and international communication, stereotypes in international relations, contentious politics, charismatic leadership and leadership in international business. Lectures are combined with workshops, exercises and internships, in classes built around discussion with experienced staff. Graduates are prepared for diplomatic and consular offices, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other public institutions, as well as international companies.

needs.note: Scores up to 40 of 100 pts; civics, or any other subject at a lower weight, can fill this slot
A modern foreign language scores up to 20 of 100 pts

programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on IB grades as Matura %: native language 30, foreign language 20, history or other subject 50 of 100; B2 English. 75 places in 2026. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Liberal Arts and Sciences
programmes.about: A European liberal arts degree: core courses in philosophy, logic, research methods and academic writing, disciplinary courses from biology to history, Greek and Latin, and electives from other AMU faculties.
programmes.overview: Core courses in philosophy, research methodology, logic and academic writing run alongside English throughout the three years, with the chance to take ancient Greek and Latin. Disciplinary courses draw on biology, physics, geography, political science and history, and from the second year you choose one course from this programme and two from other university faculties. The programme is part of the European Consortium of Liberal Arts and Sciences. Graduates are described as having analytical and communication skills useful in business, academia, government and the nonprofit sector, and many go on to study medicine, law or education.
programmes.ib: An interview on one of two topics you propose (pass mark 60 of 100) counts alongside your IB grades.

needs.note: A modern foreign language scores up to 30 of 100 grade points

programmes.selectionNote: Interview (100 pts, at least 60) plus IB grades as Matura % (100: native language 20, foreign language 30, any subject 50); B2 English. 40 places in 2026. 2026 criteria.

programmes.name: Global Communication
programmes.about: Linguistics, literature and communication studies across the English-speaking and East Slavic worlds: English and Russian to B2+ level, plus an optional third language (Spanish, German, Belarusian or Ukrainian).
programmes.overview: The programme covers linguistics, literary studies, culture and communication studies, with language training in English, Russian and a third language of your choice: Spanish, German, Belarusian or Ukrainian. Alongside lectures there are exercises, conversation classes, laboratories and workshops. Graduates work in international organisations and public administration, NGOs and foundations, cultural institutions, international firms, marketing and publishing, and in logistics or customer service roles for companies serving Central and Eastern European markets. A second-cycle degree is open to those continuing in fields that need English, Russian and another foreign language.

needs.note: Scores 70 of 100 pts; only an HL grade counts

programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on IB grades as Matura %: English HL 70, native language 30 of 100; B2 English. 30 places in the 2026 first round. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Applied Linguistics and Intercultural Communication
programmes.about: Using languages in multicultural settings: English and German grammar, contrastive linguistics, public speaking and intercultural training, with German from the start and a third language (Spanish or French).
programmes.overview: English and German are studied together, with descriptive grammar of each, contrastive grammar of the two languages, introductory linguistics and text and discourse linguistics. A cultural-communication strand covers public speaking, intercultural competence training and multilingualism and multiculturalism in the European Union. You also take a third language, Spanish or French. Graduates work in international and multicultural organisations, public relations, advertising and creative agencies, translation offices and travel agencies.
programmes.ib: Taught in English and German; German starts from zero, and English at B1 or above is required.

needs.note: Scores 70 of 100 pts; only an HL grade counts
Best one scores 30 of 100 pts; only HL counts

programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on IB HL grades as Matura %: English 70, plus geography, history, maths or another foreign language 30 of 100. 25 places in 2026. 2026 criteria.

programmes.name: Governance of Organizations
programmes.about: Leading and managing organisations, drawing on political science, law and communication: ESG, compliance, conflict management and AI tools, plus an intensive foreign language (preferably German) to B2.
programmes.overview: The curriculum draws on three areas: political science and administration, law, and communication and media. Project work and soft-skills classes build abilities such as conflict management, argumentation and public speaking, including the use of AI, and an intensive foreign-language course, preferably German, is included. You also learn about ESG, compliance management and political and business communication. Graduates can work in government agencies, administrative bodies and EU institutions, or in businesses, foundations, associations and NGOs, and the degree leads on to master's courses in Poland and abroad.

needs.note: A modern foreign language scores up to 70 of 100 pts; HL weighs more
Up to 30 of 100 pts; civics or any other subject can fill this slot at a lower weight

programmes.selectionNote: Ranked on IB grades as Matura %: foreign language 70, history or another subject 30 of 100; B2 English. 25 places in the 2026 first round. 2026 criteria.

notes: English-taught fees are the same for every student, EU citizens and Poles included; EU citizens study free only on Polish-taught degrees.
Where the formula counts Polish, your native language takes its place; an HL grade counts as extended level and weighs up to double an SL grade.
AMU does not publish past points thresholds; programmes with places left reopen in later rounds over the summer.
